chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the crucified one, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that my grandfather (peace be upon him) prayed Salat upon his uncle?' I said, 'I know that, but I do not understand it clearly.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I shall clarify it for you. If the face of the crucified one was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his right shoulder; and if his back was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his left shoulder. For indeed, between the East and the West is the Qiblah. And if his left shoulder was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his right shoulder, and if his right shoulder was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his left shoulder. And however he was inclined, do not cease to be by his shoulder, and let your face be towards what is between the East and the West, and do not face towards him nor face away from his back completely.' Abu Hashim said, 'And I have understood it, Allah willing! I understood it, by Allah!'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: Prayer (specifically funeral prayer in this context)

ai.seo_question: How to position the Imam for funeral prayer when the deceased is crucified?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of Salat al-Janazah for a crucified person, emphasizing that the Imam should stand by the shoulder and face the general direction between East and West to avoid directly facing or turning his back to the deceased. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of maintaining respect and proper orientation during funeral prayers, even when the body's position is irregular or elevated. The detailed instructions highlight the importance of precision in ritual practice, ensuring that the prayer is performed in accordance with the principles of Qiblah and bodily dignity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary who said,

‘I asked Al-Rezaasws about the crucified one. So heasws said: ‘But, do you know that myasws grandfatherasws prayed Salaat upon hisasws uncle?’ I said, ‘I know that, but I do not understand it clearly’. Heasws said: ‘Iasws shall clarify it for you. If the face of the crucified one was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his right shoulder; and if his back towards the Qiblah, so stand by his left shoulder. So if the Qiblah was between the east and the west, and if his left shoulder was towards the Qiblah, so stand upon his right shoulder, and if his right shoulder was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his left shoulder. And howsoever he was inclined, do not cease to be by his shoulder, and let your face be towards what is between the east and the west, and do not face towards him nor face away from his back’. Abu Hashim (the narrator) said, ‘And I have understood it, Allahazwj Willing! I understood it, by Allahazwj!’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from abu Hashim al-Ja‘fariy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about one who is crucified. He (the Imam) said, ‘Do you not know that my grandfather performed Salah (prayer) for his uncle?’ I said, ‘I know it but I do not understand it clearly.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘I explain it for you. If the face of the person crucified is toward al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah), stand near his right shoulder. If his back is toward al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah), then stand near his left shoulder but if it is between the east and west and his left shoulder toward al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah), then stand near his right shoulder. If his right shoulder is toward al- Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah), then stand near his left shoulder. To whichever direction he is, do not keep away from his shoulders and keep your face toward east or west, and do not stand face to face with him. You must not turn your back to him.’ Abu Hashim has said that I then said, ‘I certainly understood, by the will of Allah, I understood it by Allah.’”
